record.paper_title: Some Open Problems and Conjectures on Submanifolds of Finite Type: Recent Development
record.original_question: Classify all hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in Eⁿ⁺² whose position vector field is of finite type, meaning that it decomposes into a finite sum of Laplace eigenmaps plus a constant vector.

evidence.quote: The immersion x is said to be of finite type if the position vector field of M in E^m... can be expressed as a finite sum of E^m-valued eigenfunctions of the Laplace operator.
Problem 3. Classify finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere in E^(n+2).
The classification of k-type spherical hypersurfaces with k ≥ 3 remains a very challenge problem.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{n+1}(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ denote the standard hypersphere of radius $r$ centered at the origin in Euclidean $(n+2)$-space. Let $x : M^n \to S^{n+1}(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ be an isometric immersion of a connected $n$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M^n$ as a hypersurface of $S^{n+1}(r)$, and let $\Delta$ denote the Laplace-Beltrami operator of $M^n$ acting componentwise on $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$-valued functions.

The immersion $x$ is said to be of finite type (more precisely, of $k$-type) if its position vector field admits a decomposition
$$x = c + x_1 + x_2 + \cdots + x_k,$$
where $c \in \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ is a constant vector and $x_1, \dots, x_k$ are non-constant $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$-valued maps on $M^n$ satisfying
$$\Delta x_i = \lambda_i x_i, \qquad i = 1, \dots, k,$$
with pairwise distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k$.

Problem: Classify, up to rigid motion of $\mathbb{E}^{n+2}$, all hypersurfaces $M^n$ of the hypersphere $S^{n+1}(r) \subset \mathbb{E}^{n+2}$ whose position vector field is of finite type in the above sense. In particular, classify all $k$-type spherical hypersurfaces for every $k \geq 3$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open in general. Only the 1-type case (Takahashi's theorem characterizing minimal submanifolds of hyperspheres) and partial results in the 2-type case (under additional curvature or principal-curvature hypotheses by Chen, Ferrández–Lucas, and others) are known. The classification of $k$-type spherical hypersurfaces for $k\geq 3$ is widely cited as a challenging open problem with no general resolution to date.

status_evidence.title: Some open problems and conjectures on submanifolds of finite type: recent development
status_evidence.snippet: Lists classification of finite type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere as an open problem; states the k≥3 case remains a very challenging problem.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is explicitly listed as open, with the k≥3 case noted as a very challenging open problem.

status_evidence.title: Local rigidity theorems of 2-type hypersurfaces in a hypersphere
status_evidence.snippet: Obtains partial classification/rigidity results for 2-type hypersurfaces of a hypersphere.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results known for the 2-type case.

status_evidence.title: Riemannian Submanifolds: A Survey (B.-Y. Chen)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses finite-type submanifolds; classification of higher-type spherical hypersurfaces remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Survey indicates the general classification has not been completed.
